investigation.title: Remote Agents: Swarm Gateway 502 Blocking All Agent Provisioning Evals
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents feature checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-10-14T12:36–12:37Z with an identical 502 bad_gateway error indicating the swarm provisioning gateway — an AWS ELB in us-east-2 — was unreachable when the eval runner called POST /api/agents. Because the failure is shared across every sibling check with the same error message and zero evidence was collected, the fault is localized to the shared upstream swarm gateway dependency, not to any individual check's logic.
investigation.rootCause: The swarm gateway (an AWS ELB in us-east-2 fronting the /v1/agents provisioning endpoint) returned a 502 bad_gateway to the production-api layer when the eval runner issued POST /api/agents. This caused the request to fail before any agent identity, VM ID, or remote state could be established, leaving all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) absent. The identical error message and timing across all three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) is consistent with a shared upstream dependency failure rather than a per-check code defect. No historical run data is available to establish a regression baseline, and no suspect code changes are identified in sourceDiscovery.suspectChanges, so the cause is localized to the swarm gateway / ELB infrastructure layer at the time of the eval run.
